title: Limited Drop Alert Video Template | AIVideosUGC
description: Make a short alert video for a small release or restock from one product photo. After you download it, add the date, the quantity, and your link.
h1: Limited Drop Alert Video for a Restock or Small Release
lead: Tell shoppers the coral trail shoes are back, without a new fitting. Put the pair in an alert frame. An AI avatar wears the color you photographed.
steps_h2: Make a Limited Release Ad in 3 Steps
steps_lead: Leave with an alert you can post: open the frame, add the coral shoes and the sentence, and download the clip.

steps.d: The frame is already a short alert for one pair. You can say the coral shoes are back without holding a fitting.
Use a photo of the pair that returned, or the product page link. Add the date, the count, and the buy link after download.
Captions can carry the restock sentence while the coral shoes stay on screen, and you do not wait on a crew.

faq.q: What does a drop alert template include?
faq.a: A short alert frame for a restock, such as coral trail shoes that just returned. The photographed color is the one that appears. You can say the pair is back without booking a person to wear them.

faq.q: What do I do to turn the template into an alert?
faq.a: Start from the color that actually came back. An AI actor speaks the alert while the coral shoes stay in frame, and you post that clip to people shopping the restock.

faq.q: What kinds of products can a drop alert show?
faq.a: A restocked pair of trail shoes, or another item you can photograph and ship. The shoes in the photo are the pair that returned. Leave out a color you cannot ship.

faq.q: Can I cut several alerts for one drop?
faq.a: Yes. The same coral shoes can get a tall alert for a phone and a second sentence for shoppers who only want that color. You keep the photo and change the sentence.

faq.q: Who is a drop alert like this for?
faq.a: A label that brings pairs back in small piles and cannot stop for a fitting. The person who writes the caption can also make the clip.

faq.q: Can I send a drop alert if I have never cut a video?
faq.a: Yes. Photograph the coral shoes and type the line, even if you have never edited a video.

faq.q: When is the alert file in my hands?
faq.a: When the render finishes. You can post the shoe alert in that same work session, with no fitting on the calendar.

A clip spends 24 credits for 6 seconds, 40 for 10, 60 for 15, and 120 for 30. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600. If the job fails, those credits return. The file has no watermark.

faq.q: When do I add the date, the count, and the link?
faq.a: After download, in the editor. The template does not invent a date or a quantity for the shoes.

faq.q: Where can I post the alert?
faq.a: On TikTok, Instagram, or Facebook, in a tall, square, or wide frame, plus 4:3 and 3:4. Use the shoe alert in ads and on the product page, inside your plan's license.

reviews.h2: How Shops Make a Release Alert
reviews.lead: Examples of how a shop makes a short release alert. You still add the date and the quantity after download.

items.t: A finished alert from one product photo
items.d: Example: a watch shop uploads a photo of the watch and gets a short alert it can post. The release date is typed on later.

items.t: The still and the clip in one project
items.d: Example: an apparel shop builds the jacket photo and the restock alert together, in one project, without a second app.

items.t: Hold the pair, or start from the link
items.d: Example: a shoe shop pastes the product page link, or uploads the pair, and the clip shows those shoes held up for the release.

items.t: An AI actor, then captions in the editor
items.d: Example: the shop picks an AI actor, a generated person, to hold the jacket. It trims the clip in the editor and adds words on screen.

items.t: The same drop in another language
items.d: Example: a beauty shop keeps one color reveal and speaks the line again in a second language for the other market.

items.t: A track and a spoken line before download
items.d: Example: a home shop adds a spoken voice and a music track, then edits both before the candle restock goes out.

items.t: An AI actor for a small release
items.d: Example: a bag shop uses an AI actor, a generated person, to show a small release. Someone new to video can start from one photo.

items.t: Same generated person, no new lights
items.d: Example: a drink shop uses a digital twin, the same generated person, for each new can. The team does not set up lights again.

items.t: A script, a voice, and a second version
items.d: Example: a jewelry shop pastes the product link, takes the words and the spoken voice, then makes a second version from the same photo.

items.t: Post to TikTok or Meta, or use the API
items.d: Example: a fitness shop posts the gear alert to TikTok or Meta (Facebook and Instagram). The API lets the store's product list start the next alert.
